headline: Fixed-SAE Track traces bounded, format-heavy RL shifts in a small reasoning model
summary: A September 14, 2026 arXiv paper introduces Fixed-SAE Track: it trains one shared sparse autoencoder per analyzed layer on activations pooled across a base model and its RL checkpoints, then freezes the feature directions to track representation shifts. In the main Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct math-RL setting, the authors report gradual late-layer drift concentrated in formatting and reasoning scaffolds. Steering amplified features at dose α=10 raises strict accuracy from 0.050 to 0.192, close to the short-RL final model’s 0.175, while lenient reasoning accuracy changes more modestly. The paper also reports that all 29 selected GSM8K problems that shift from greedy-base-wrong to RL-right are solved by base sampling at k=64; however, 2000 additional RL steps raise lenient accuracy from 0.300 to 0.408, and directly injecting a necessary reasoning feature set recovers little. The approximately 80% headline therefore concerns a bounded short-RL extractability/format effect, not a general claim that RL only elicits existing capability. Results are author-reported and not independently reproduced.
